node.title: Re: Using Timestamp to tell if someone is on the site
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [htmanning],

I often recommend something like [mod://DateTime] for such calculations, but since in this case you're just subtracting two times to tell if they're more or less than 5 minutes apart and you probably don't need high precision, probably the easiest way is with UNIX timestamps, as [huck] [id://1178977|suggested]. In Perl, you can use [doc://time] to get seconds since the epoch (which on most systems is January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC), and depending on the format of the database column, you can either have the database convert that to a UNIX timestamp, e.g. MySQL has the function UNIX_TIMESTAMP(date), or, if you've stored it in the database as a string, you can use [doc://Time::Piece]::strptime, [mod://POSIX::strptime], or [mod://DateTime::Format::Strptime] to parse it back into seconds since the epoch - just don't forget to [id://1178137|take time zones into account]. Then, it's just a simple matter of subtraction of the two values.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
